publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/failLoudGuards.test.ts (10), mutation-verified. Three crons change here and BOTH changes move a guard from fail-OPEN to fail-CLOSED on the non-operator path. (1) QUIET HOURS. confirmationCalls.ts and voiceRecovery.ts each inlined their own ET-hour extraction with a bare parseInt. NaN fails every comparison, so the expression "etHour < 15 || etHour >= 18" evaluates FALSE and the window guard let outbound calling through at any hour. The two NAMED copies (reviewRequests.ts:116, followupCadence.ts:63) already carried the isFinite-else-0 fallback and held. All four now share getBusinessHour() in lib/timezoneAssert.ts, whose docstring already described this exact class. The test asserts the fallback against all four REAL windows (15-18, 10-17, 9-19, 9-18) rather than against the literal 0, so a future window spanning midnight cannot silently turn the fallback into an open door. Mutation: reverting the fallback to a bare parseInt turns 3 tests red. (2) PLACES REJECTION. reviewMonitor.ts fetches Google Places, which signals REQUEST_DENIED inside a 200 body. The response.ok guard cannot see it, so result was empty, reviews was empty, and the job returned recordsProcessed:0 with details "No reviews returned from API" and SUCCEEDED — a denied credential presented to the operator as the shop having no new reviews, with a completed cron_log row. It now throws, landing a failed row the failure observer can see. Guard added at the shared client (_core/map.ts) so gbp-reviews.ts and competitorMonitor inherit it. ZERO_RESULTS asserted NOT to throw. Mutation: neutering the status check turns 3 tests red. NO operator is in either loop, which is why the direction matters: neither cron has anyone to notice a wrong answer.

operator-walkthrough.ref: LIVE — three operator surfaces change and all three are visible without a deploy step. (1) Settings > Feature Flags. The confirmation now fires on the direction that can REACH CUSTOMERS. For sms_global_pause and vapi_forward_followup_paused — OFF-switches, where TRUE pauses — that direction is OFF. Flipping the shop-wide SMS pause ON is now silent; turning it OFF raises "Resume automated sending?" with buttons [Resume sending] / [Stay paused]. Previously it was backwards: engaging the kill switch raised a red modal claiming it would send to real customers, with the cancel button labelled "Keep OFF" — the reassuring button resumed sending. The amber chip tooltip on those two rows now reads OFF-SWITCH rather than the generic customer-facing text. (2) Winback > SMS Orchestrator. APPROVE & SEND, REJECT and DISMISS disable while the mutation is in flight and the primary button reads SENDING... The server has no repeat guard and passes humanInitiated:true (which exempts the send from takeover suppression), so a double-tap on shop wifi previously sent the same customer the same text twice. (3) Outreach > SMS thread view. Send Draft disables in flight and reads Sending... — matching the reply composer 87 lines below it, which was already gated with the same mutation object. Nothing new to learn: no new screens, no moved controls, and the only copy change is on the two off-switches, where the old copy was wrong.

capability-ledger-updated.ref: capability-ledger.json: first-party-evidence-ingestion updated (lastVerifiedAt 2026-07-17 -> 2026-08-03; evidence.tests added; blocker text and deferredScope rewritten). That is the capability this diff actually touches — its P1 has read "prod evidence tables EMPTY ... Places key REQUEST_DENIED" since the 2026-07-17 live probe, and the reason it read as "tables empty" instead of "credential denied" is the defect fixed here: the cron swallowed the rejection and reported success. DELIBERATELY NOT PROMOTED. operationalState stays unverified and exposure stays disabled. This PR makes the failure LOUD; it does not make reviews flow. The operator GCP fix is still the only thing that unblocks ingestion, and promoting on a visibility fix would put a false verification date on a capability that has never ingested a row. The blocker now records that distinction explicitly, and deferredScope records what the first honest signal will be: a FAILED cron_log row for review-monitor rather than a silent completed one.
